ambiguity_notes: Spec says 'release of reset is synchronous to clk' but reset itself is asynchronous active-low; I interpreted this as: the rst_n=0 assertion is asynchronous (immediately clears done and FSM), but the deassertion (rst_n going back to 1) is only sampled on a rising clock edge to avoid metastability.

Spec says encryption 'auto-starts on cycle the 144th bit is shifted in'; I assumed this means the first round computation occurs on the same clock edge that latches the 144th bit, i.e., load and round-1 share that clock edge.
Spec does not specify what happens if load_en is asserted during the ENCRYPT phase; I assumed it aborts encryption and restarts the LOAD phase, consistent with the 'done clears on new load' rule.

Spec does not specify what happens if shift_out_en is deasserted mid-unload; I assumed the unload pauses (bit counter freezes) and resumes when shift_out_en is reasserted, without losing the partial output position.
Spec does not specify the reset value of state[63:0] or key_reg[79:0]; I assumed they are undefined after reset and only become valid after a complete 144-cycle load.
Spec does not specify the reset value of dout; I assumed it is driven to 0 after reset.
The spec states done is 'held high until reset or new load begins'; I assumed 'new load begins' means the first rising edge where load_en is sampled high, at which point done clears synchronously.

Spec does not explicitly state whether the key schedule update for round i uses the round counter value before or after incrementing; I assumed the counter value i (1..31) used in the XOR into key_reg[19:15] corresponds to the round just completed, consistent with the PRESENT-80 standard.
Spec does not define FSM state encoding; I assumed one-hot encoding as a reasonable default for a small FSM targeting 30% utilisation.

The spec says 'P(i) = (i×16) mod 63 for i=0..62; P(63)=63' — this is the destination index of source bit i; I assumed P(i) is the destination position of source bit i (i.e., bit i of the input goes to position P(i) of the output), consistent with the PRESENT specification.

behavior_invariants.condition: While load_en is asserted, on each rising edge of clk the internal shift register {key_reg[79:0], state[63:0]} shifts left by one bit and din is inserted at the LSB position, so that after exactly 144 rising edges the first 80 bits received become key_reg and the next 64 bits become state (plaintext). The bit received first occupies the MSB of key_reg.
behavior_invariants.description: During load phase, each rising clock edge while load_en is high shifts din into the MSB of the combined {key_reg, state} shift register
behavior_invariants.name: load_phase_serial_shift

behavior_invariants.condition: On the rising clock edge at which the internal load bit counter reaches 144, the FSM transitions from LOAD to ENCRYPT and begins round 1 of the PRESENT-80 algorithm on that same cycle, without waiting for an additional clock.
behavior_invariants.description: Encryption begins automatically on the clock cycle that the 144th bit is shifted in, without any external trigger
behavior_invariants.name: encrypt_auto_start

behavior_invariants.condition: For each round i from 1 to 31, in a single clock cycle: (1) state is XORed with key_reg[79:16]; (2) the 4-bit S-box S={C,5,6,B,9,0,A,D,3,E,F,8,4,7,1,2} is applied independently to each of the 16 nibbles of state; (3) the pLayer permutation P(i)=(i*16) mod 63 for i=0..62 and P(63)=63 is applied to state; (4) key_reg is rotated left by 61 bits, the top nibble of key_reg is substituted through the same S-box, and the 5-bit round counter i is XORed into key_reg[19:15].
behavior_invariants.description: Each encryption clock cycle executes exactly one full PRESENT-80 round: addRoundKey, sBoxLayer, pLayer, then key schedule update
behavior_invariants.name: encrypt_round_sequence

behavior_invariants.condition: On the 32nd encryption clock cycle (after 31 full rounds), state is XORed with key_reg[79:16] (the round-32 subkey) and no further sBoxLayer, pLayer, or key schedule update is performed. The result is the ciphertext stored in state[63:0].
behavior_invariants.description: After round 31, one additional addRoundKey is applied to produce the final ciphertext
behavior_invariants.name: final_add_round_key

behavior_invariants.condition: done is set to 1 on the rising clock edge that completes the 32nd encryption cycle (final addRoundKey). done remains 1 until either rst_n is deasserted (asynchronous clear) or load_en is asserted to begin a new load sequence, whichever comes first.
behavior_invariants.description: done is asserted exactly when the final addRoundKey completes and held high until reset or a new load begins
behavior_invariants.name: done_assertion

behavior_invariants.condition: On each rising clock edge where both done and shift_out_en are asserted, the MSB of the internal ciphertext shift register is presented on dout and the register shifts left by one bit. The first bit output is state[63] (MSB of ciphertext) and the 64th bit output is state[0] (LSB of ciphertext).
behavior_invariants.description: While done is high and shift_out_en is high, ciphertext is shifted out MSB-first on dout at one bit per clock
behavior_invariants.name: unload_serial_shift

behavior_invariants.condition: Whenever rst_n transitions to 0, regardless of clk, done is immediately driven to 0, the FSM returns to idle, and all in-progress load, encrypt, or unload operations are abandoned. The internal state and key_reg values after reset are undefined until a new load sequence completes.
behavior_invariants.description: Asserting rst_n low asynchronously clears done and aborts any in-progress operation
behavior_invariants.name: async_reset_behavior

behavior_invariants.condition: If load_en is asserted while done is high, done is cleared on the next rising clock edge and the FSM transitions to the LOAD state, discarding the previous ciphertext and beginning a fresh 144-cycle serial load.
behavior_invariants.description: Asserting load_en while done is high clears done and begins a new load sequence
behavior_invariants.name: load_en_restarts_operation

behavior_invariants.condition: The value on dout is only architecturally meaningful when both done and shift_out_en are simultaneously asserted. At all other times dout may be 0 or hold its last driven value and must not be interpreted as valid ciphertext.
behavior_invariants.description: dout carries valid ciphertext data only when done is high and shift_out_en is high
behavior_invariants.name: dout_valid_only_during_unload

behavior_invariants.condition: For the four key/plaintext pairs (key=0x00000000000000000000, pt=0x0000000000000000 → ct=0x5579C1387B228445), (key=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, pt=0x0000000000000000 → ct=0xE72C46C0F5945049), (key=0x00000000000000000000, pt=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF → ct=0xA112FFC72F68417B), (key=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, pt=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF → ct=0x3333DCD3213210D2), the ciphertext in state[63:0] after the 32nd encryption cycle must exactly match the specified values.
behavior_invariants.description: The module must produce the four specified PRESENT-80 test vector ciphertexts
behavior_invariants.name: test_vector_correctness

clock_domains.name: clk
clock_domains.notes: Single clock domain; all registers clocked on rising edge; 10 ns target period on gf180mcuD PDK

port_assumptions.notes: Rising-edge triggered; 100 MHz target, 10 ns period
Asynchronous active-low reset; release is synchronous to clk
Must be held high for exactly 144 consecutive rising edges to complete a full load; asserting it mid-encrypt or mid-unload restarts the load phase
Serial input; sampled on rising clk edge while load_en is high; key MSB (bit 79) arrives first, plaintext MSB (bit 63) arrives on cycle 81
Only effective when done is also asserted; may be deasserted mid-unload to pause output
Ciphertext MSB (state[63]) is the first bit shifted out; valid only when done and shift_out_en are both high
Asserted after 32 encrypt cycles complete; cleared asynchronously by rst_n=0 or synchronously by load_en assertion
